uncited: Half-Space Field Generation creates a binary volume representation by assigning a value of 1 to voxels within a defined region (typically the fluid domain) and 0 to those outside, effectively masking simulation or rendering computations.
It differs from continuous implicit primitives by discretizing the domain boundary into a hard binary mask rather than evaluating a smooth scalar field for isosurface extraction.
- Input: A 3D grid domain defined by dimensions $(xSize, ySize, zSize)$ and a logical condition defining the "inside" region (e.g., $y > ySize/2$ or $\phi < 0$).
Iterate through the voxel coordinates $(x, y, z)$ where $0 \le x < xSize$, $0 \le z < zSize$.
For general level-set based generation, evaluate the level set function $\phi(\vec{x})$.
Use the resulting binary mask in shaders or solvers to gate computations.
- **GPU Flow Control:** Checking the level set value in shaders requires dynamic flow control.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ where $N = xSize \times ySize \times zSize$, as every voxel must be visited to set the binary value.
The technique is widely used in real-time fluid simulation to define the domain of the solver.
